executives.name: Elon Musk
executives.title: Technoking of Tesla & Chief Executive Officer

prepared_remarks.speaker: Elon Musk
prepared_remarks.text: In Q3 2024, Tesla delivered over 462,000 vehicles and achieved record energy storage deployments of 6.9 GWh. Cost of goods sold per vehicle decreased to its lowest level ever at ~$35,100. Our focus remains on vehicle affordability, Full Self-Driving (FSD) supervised rollouts, and autonomous transport. We are on track to launch more affordable models in the first half of 2025.

prepared_remarks.speaker: Vaibhav Taneja
prepared_remarks.text: Automotive gross margin excluding regulatory credits was 17.1%, expanding sequentially by 250 bps. Regulatory credit revenue was $739 million. Free cash flow was strong at $2.74 billion, supported by disciplined operational expenditure even as AI compute CapEx reached $1.5 billion in the quarter. Total cash and investments rose to $33.6B.

qa_session.question: Elon, can you discuss the regulatory approval timeline for unsupervised FSD in Texas and California, and how competitive pricing pressures in China are impacting your margin outlook?

answers.speaker: Elon Musk
answers.text: For FSD, we expect to be offering paid driverless Cybercab rides in Texas next year, and in California subject to regulatory approval. Regarding competition in China, the EV landscape is extremely fierce, but our manufacturing efficiency and software autonomy stack create a sustainable cost and utility advantage.

answers.speaker: Vaibhav Taneja
answers.text: We continue to manage localized price elasticity dynamically. Raw material deflation and localized supply chains in Shanghai provide a meaningful buffer against localized price wars.

qa_session.question: Could you provide guidance on 2025 delivery volume growth, and what are the specific bottlenecks in the 4680 battery cell ramp and Cybertruck production?

answers.speaker: Elon Musk
answers.text: Subject to global macroeconomic conditions and no major disruptions, my best estimate is that vehicle delivery growth could reach 20% to 30% next year. The Cybertruck has already achieved positive gross margin in Q3. 4680 cell production is ramping rapidly and approaching cost parity with our primary suppliers.

guidance_summary.delivery_growth_outlook: 20% to 30% projected delivery growth in FY25
guidance_summary.capex_guidance: Expected to exceed $10 billion in FY24 driven by AI datacenter infrastructure
guidance_summary.energy_business: Energy storage deployments expected to more than double year-over-year in FY24
